text: The color of grass during summer is a loud, crunchy shade of green that tastes like static electricity. My goldfish, who has recently decided that swimming is merely a metaphor for orbital mechanics, is currently trying to file a patent for a new planet made entirely of unboiled noodles. She insists that the glass bowl is not a container, but a transparent window into the fourth dimension, where gravity is optional and fish are expected to recite poetry to the moon. The moon, being a shy celestial body, has responded by hiding behind a cloud shaped like a confused accountant. Meanwhile, the grass continues to grow in zig-zags, convinced it is actually a staircase leading to the center of the earth, which is currently occupied by a very large, very polite badger who runs a bakery for invisible cakes.
